top_reviews.review_title: AWESOME DEAL AND NICHROME IS NOT KANTHAL!
top_reviews.review_text:
I was looking to repair a kiln.  I thought nichrome was the right wire.  It worked for a little while but nichrome tarnished more than kanthal.  At least that is what I figured out from the internet.However this nichrome is really nice.  Apparently it is meant for things that heat up fast and for shorter periods of time.The nichrome is good for an incredible amount of heat.  So I got this sample pack to use as tie wire and to fix smaller appliances like hair dryer or heat guns.  The wire appears to be American made and supplied.The company also sells Kanthal wire too!  So I bought a bunch of this to fix my mistake.  To be clear the nichrome wire might have worked.  I had wrapped the broken wires (they were cast in refractory cement) around a stainless steel m3 bolt and nut.  I wrapped the nichrome around that and then cast them into newly repaired refractory.  All of my connections failed by going higher resistance.  I would assume the nichrome might have worked if I had used ONLY nichrome and had no connections to the unknown existing wire.The wire is very consistent and measured out at the resistances I expected.  I will try to use the thinner wires to wire-wrap the connections with plenty of overlap between the old wire and the new Kanthal.  Since I don't care about continuity between the nichrome and anything else the different in material shouldn't matter since it is there for mechanical binding only.
